evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: B00037, research note and linked historical dictionary readings
evidence.text: The entry records 体 with two separate readings and histories: bèn, glossed from Guangyun as “coarse; inferior” and analyzed by the dictionary editor as 人 semantic plus 本 phonetic; and tǐ, treated as a variant of 體. It cites Longkan Shoujian and other historical dictionaries for the bèn entry. This supports keeping the lexical uses distinct; it does not establish that the bèn word developed into the tǐ form.
evidence.title: [B00037] 体 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry classifies 体 as a vulgar variant of 體, citing historical dictionaries and examples from Song-Yuan onward in which 體 is written 体. It separately notes the bèn reading and says 体 also functions as an independently indexed character. The entry supports variant status but does not document the exact route by which this shape became standardized simplified Chinese.
evidence.title: [A04666] 體 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, reproducing Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.field: 體 entry, definition and form analysis
evidence.text: The page reproduces Shuowen’s account: 體 means a set of twelve bodily divisions and is formed from 骨 with 豊 as phonetic. Duan Yucai later elaborates the twelve divisions. This is an early lexicographic analysis, not independent confirmation of the character’s original formation. No matching 豊 reconstruction was verified here.
evidence.title: 說文解字「體」 - Shuowen.org

evidence.field: File summary, original file and licensing
evidence.text: The Commons file page identifies 體-seal.svg as a small seal-script form based on the Shuowen-style source designation S02964. The uploader’s vector is a modern redraw, not a photograph of an ancient artifact. The page marks the ancient-script vector as public domain and provides an original-file link.

gaps: No exact earliest dated attestation for 體 or 体 was established. The consulted evidence does not provide a secure first-occurrence chronology.

The dictionary’s analysis of bèn 体 as 人 semantic plus 本 phonetic is an editorial account; early paleographic evidence for that analysis was not inspected. The tǐ spelling is independently recorded as a variant of 體.
The historical semantic bridge, if any, between 体 bèn “coarse; inferior” and 体 tǐ as a spelling of 體 remains unestablished; do not conflate them.
The Shuowen source asserts 豊 is phonetic in 體, but this research did not verify a 豊 pronunciation and 體 pronunciation comparison within the same reconstruction system.

The local task data gives modern Mandarin tǐ for both 体 and 體 and Baxter–Sagart 體 *r̥ˤijʔ (MC thejX), with no supplied Baxter–Sagart rows for 体 or 本. These repository rows are not external evidence. Official Unihan pages were inaccessible.
Commons page for 体-seal.svg could not be inspected. An alternate exact image source was not established for that shape.

The 體 seal image is a modern vector redraw in seal-script style; it is not a photograph of an excavated artifact and cannot substantiate early dating. No Xiaoxuetang character-specific glyph image was verified.
